text:
incident-bot: ALERT: high rate of CUDA_ALLOC_FAILURE on gpu-pool-east2a (threshold 50/min)
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident PDR-8742 created and paged eng-oncall-primary (severity: high)
Alex: ack'd oncall page, I'm looking
Lee: joining, switching to this channel — oncall handover from night shift
Jamie: FYI metrics show KV cache evictions spiked at 16:12 UTC, started ~15:58 after rollout of kv-prefetch tuning
Alex: logs show repeated 'E_CUDA_OUT_OF_MEMORY' from infer-worker-42 and infer-worker-47
Alex: running quick top/gpu checks, also noticing small surge in running seq len on requests
Ryan: customer telemetry: one Dedicated customer (acme-inc) seeing 5-10% increased error rate on generation endpoints
Emma: putting customer comms on standby, will draft if we see sustained impact
Lee: can we drain the most affected nodes? runbook step: cordon+evacuate pool-east2a nodes with >80% alloc failures
Jamie: running evac script now: `./ops/evacuate_gpu_pool --pool east2a --threshold 0.8`
pagerduty-bot: Pager acknowledged by Alex (oncall)
Alex: evac started, draining 2 nodes (id: gpu-42, gpu-47). If drain succeeds, fallback routing will send traffic to warm spare pool
Ryan: confirming path: hosted API will fallback to compat-model-1 (slower but stable) during evacuation
Lee: tracing KV prefetcher config from the rollout: `kv_prefetch.window=128 -> 512` and `prefetch_concurrency=8 -> 24` changed at 15:55 UTC
Jamie: reverting concurrency to 8 on a test node to validate
Alex: quick mitigation tests: 1) reduce prefetch concurrency 2) force KV cache warm hit reuse 3) reduce batch size for model-1
Jamie: test revert on worker-99: prefetch_concurrency=8 -> memory stable, no OOMs for 10m
Lee: good signal. rolling a targeted config rollback to pool-east2a (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%)
Alex: coordinating with scheduler to throttle new allocations to the pool while rollback proceeds
Emma: drafting note: "We observed transient GPU memory pressure after a kv-prefetch tuning change. We are rolling back the tuning and evacuating affected hosts. No widespread customer data exposure." Will hold for ops confirm
Ryan: customer impact update: ACME request failure rate peaked at 9% but is down to 3% after initial drain, monitoring
Alex: handoff: I'll stay on until rollback hits 100% and we confirm stable error rate <0.5% for 15m. Lee, if anything spikes, escalate to SRE lead @Jamie
Lee: ack. If rollback fails, prepare for temporary autoscale of warm spare pool (requesting +4 GPUs)
pagerduty-bot: Escalation timer set — will escalate to eng-sre-lead in 12m if unacked by then
incident-bot: runbook step completed: evacuated 2 nodes, rollback canary at 10% applied at 16:02 UTC
Jamie: monitoring kv_evictions, cuda_alloc_errors, and tail latencies (prom dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood/pool-east2a)
Alex: metrics update 16:10 UTC: cuda_alloc_failures per-min down 70% in canary hosts, overall pool error rate down 45%
Emma: customer note ready to send to ACME if they ask; holding until we hit stable 15m window
Lee: rolling to 50% now, no regressions observed in canary, moving to 100% in 5m
Alex: bumping last_message_ts as we approach full rollback, staying pinned here
Ryan: I'll call out to ACME success contact if we need to confirm service health
Alex: 16:18 UTC rollback 100% applied, starting 15m stable window timer
Jamie: setting automated monitors to alert if cuda_errors > 1/min for next 30m
Lee: thanks all — great quick ops. Postmortem: capture config change, canary gating, and add a preflight memory-simulation step to PR template
Emma: sending provisional customer note to ACME: "We've identified a server-side performance tuning change that caused transient GPU memory pressure. We've rolled back the tuning and evacuated affected hosts. Our engineering team will follow up with details."
Alex: closing PD incident when stable threshold met, will file follow-up ticket and link to this thread
pagerduty-bot: Incident PDR-8742 acknowledged and marked 'in progress'
incident-bot: NOTE: if error rate climbs again, auto-page will re-trigger. Keep monitoring. :eyes:
